title: The rule that keeps turning up

hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? who first told you to treat people the way you’d want to be treated?
options: then you’ve known this rule since before you could read. listen.
good teachers love this one. so did this teacher.
that’s the funny thing about it. it’s everywhere. listen.

steps.line: In ancient China, about 2,500 years ago, the teacher Confucius gathered students. One of the cleverest was named Zigong.
Zigong was quick, smooth-talking and very good with money. He did well as a merchant, and was sent out as a diplomat.
One day Zigong told his teacher: “What I don’t want others to do to me, I don’t want to do to them either.”

steps.q: Zigong has just said the golden rule, word for word. How does Confucius answer?
steps.why: Not yet. Zigong knew the words. Confucius wanted more than words.

steps.line: Confucius answered: “Zigong, you have not attained to that.” Not yet.

steps.q: Why would Confucius say “not yet” to a student who said exactly the right thing?
o: Saying it is easy; living it is hard
He didn’t agree with the rule
steps.why: Anyone can say it. Confucius saw it as something you grow into, day after day.

steps.line: Another day, Zigong asked: “Is there one word you could live by for your whole life?”
Confucius said: “Is not reciprocity such a word? What you do not want done to yourself, do not do to others.”

steps.q: Confucius says what not to do: don’t do what you’d hate. How is Jesus’s golden rule different?
o: It’s the same, word for word
It says what to do, not what to avoid
steps.why: Jesus: “Do to others what you would have them do to you.” Hillel, like Confucius, put it the don’t-do way.

steps.line: Today: a sharp reply typed fast, thumb over send. Would I want this sent to me? One word for a whole life, one message at a time.
steps.label: today

steps.q: Confucius told Zigong “not yet.” What did Zigong do when his teacher died?
o: Started his own school at once
Went back to trading for profit
Stayed by his grave for six years
steps.why: The other students mourned three years. Zigong built a hut by the grave and stayed three more, Mencius says. Many read it as the student living what he’d said.

say: here’s what i love. zigong said the right words, and confucius still said not yet. he wasn’t being harsh. he was saying this one takes a lifetime.

in confucian teaching the word is shu: measuring others by your own heart. what hurts you, hurts them. another student said their teacher’s whole way hung on two threads: doing your best for others, and shu.

steps.q: The written character for shu, reciprocity, joins two parts: one means “like,” the other means “heart.” From the story, why does that fit?
o: Treat people the way they treat you
Your own heart is the measure for someone else’s
Love only people who are like you
steps.why: A heart like yours. What you’d hate, they’d hate. What you’d want, they’d want.

today.say: today, before one reply or one hard conversation, ask the old question: would i want this done to me? if not, change one word. that’s shu, one message at a time.
options: good. your own heart is the map.
then you know where to start. gently.

card.keepWhy: What you would not want, don’t do.
sources: Analects 15:23 (Legge 1861): “Tsze-kung asked, saying, ‘Is there one word which may serve as a rule of practice for all one’s life?’ The Master said, ‘Is not RECIPROCITY such a word? What you do not want done to yourself, do not do to others.’” (numbered 15:24 in some editions).
Analects 5:11 (Legge 1861): “Tsze-kung said, ‘What I do not wish men to do to me, I also wish not to do to men.’ The Master said, ‘Ts’ze, you have not attained to that.’” (5:12 in some editions).
Analects 11:18 (Zigong’s goods increase); Sima Qian, Shiji 67 (Zigong as merchant and diplomat).
The character 恕 (shu), written with 如 (like, as) over 心 (heart).

Analects 4:15 (Legge 1861): Zengzi: “The doctrine of our master is to be true to the principles of our nature and the benevolent exercise of them to others” (zhong and shu, the two threads in the teach).
Day 15 script: docs/curriculum/spiritual/scripts/y1/day-0015.json (the golden rule; be good to people).
check: The order of the two scenes (5:11 and 15:23) is not known; the lesson says “one day” and “another day.” Confirm.
Zigong’s words in the 5:11 scene are lightly modernized from Legge. Confirm.
The “like + heart” reading of 恕 is traditional and widely taught (如 also gives the sound); confirm it is fair for a hard question.
Teach: “doing your best for others” renders zhong (loyalty, wholeheartedness) in Analects 4:15. Confirm the wording.
“About 2,500 years ago” for Confucius (551–479 BCE). Paintings give Confucius his traditional look, not a historical likeness.
